brief: What six years of writing online actually taught me

slots.headline: Six years of writing online, and almost none of it worked the way I expected

slots.title: Nobody owes you the second sentence
slots.body: The first line is not a warm-up, it is the whole negotiation. If it does not earn attention outright, everything underneath it is unread work. I spent two years writing careful openings that politely introduced the topic. They were skipped every time.

slots.title: Publishing beats polishing
slots.body: The pieces I agonised over for a week performed the same as the ones I wrote in an hour. What moved the needle was frequency, not finish. Consistency compounds because the audience learns when to expect you, and an audience that expects you is an audience that returns.

slots.title: Specific beats clever
slots.body: Every post that travelled had a number, a name, or a date in it. The abstract ones stayed home. Nobody shares a principle, but they will forward a receipt — the invoice, the screenshot, the exact hour it broke.

slots.title: Write for one person
slots.body: Addressing everyone produces prose that lands on no one. The posts that worked were written to a single reader I could picture — usually someone I had actually spoken to that week. The narrower the address, the wider the reach, which still feels backwards and is still true.

slots.title: The boring middle is the job
slots.body: Months eleven through thirty produced nothing worth showing anybody. No growth, no signal, no reason to continue except the decision to continue. Almost everyone quits there, which is precisely why outlasting the boring middle is most of the advantage.

slots.title: Say the thing you actually think
slots.body: Hedged writing reads as safe and performs as noise. The posts that changed anything were the ones I hesitated to press send on. If a sentence costs you nothing to publish, it probably gives the reader nothing either.

slots.headline: Six years compressed into six pages
slots.body: If any of this landed, the long version is a letter I send on Sundays. No cadence, no funnel, just the working notes.
